title: The Sunday Read: ‘What Deathbed Visions Teach Us About Living’

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 早在黑胶唱片时代的夜总会里当DJ时，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件你最珍爱的藏品去工作，把DJ台变成这样一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，里面摆满了美丽的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听来自蒂芙尼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: Hi, my name is Phoebe Zerwick and I'm a contributor to the New York Times Magazine.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我叫菲比·泽维克，我是《纽约时报杂志》的撰稿人。

sentences.en: For this week's Sunday Read, we'll be sharing a recent article for the magazine about deathbed visions.
sentences.zh: 在本周的“周日阅读”中，我们将分享一篇最近发表在杂志上关于临终幻象的文章。

sentences.en: Visions that people experience as they're dying.
sentences.zh: 人们在临终时经历的幻象。

sentences.en: These visions can begin days, weeks, maybe even months before someone passes away.
sentences.zh: 这些幻象可能在一个人去世前几天、几周，甚至几个月就开始出现。

sentences.en: And they can cover a whole range of subjects, but they tend to center on the patient's earlier life and lived experience.
sentences.zh: 它们可以涵盖各种各样的主题，但往往集中在病人早期的生活和生活经历上。

sentences.en: As death approaches, people will begin to see friends and relatives, even pets whom they loved, who preceded them in death.
sentences.zh: 随着死亡的临近，人们会开始看到先于他们离世的朋友、亲戚，甚至他们所爱过宠物。

sentences.en: People describe these deathbed visions as realer than real, as different from any other kinds of dreams that they've ever had.
sentences.zh: 人们将这些临终幻象描述为比现实更真实，与他们曾有过的任何其他类型的梦境都不同。

sentences.en: So this story is based on the research by a physician named Dr. Chris Kerr, who works at Hospice Buffalo.
sentences.zh: 所以这个故事是基于一位名叫克里斯·克尔医生的研究，他在布法罗临终关怀医院工作。

sentences.en: He believed that these deathbed visions were completely different from delusions or hallucinations brought on by medication.
sentences.zh: 他坚信这些临终幻象与药物引起的妄想或幻觉完全不同。

sentences.en: And so Kerr's team interviewed his patients and their relatives.
sentences.zh: 因此，克尔的团队采访了他的病人和他们的亲属。

sentences.en: They found that these experiences were common among a majority of patients, an astonishing 88% in their first study.
sentences.zh: 他们发现这些经历在大多数病人中很常见，在他们的第一项研究中，这一比例高达惊人的88%。

sentences.en: Dr. Kerr often says that he hasn't discovered anything new.
sentences.zh: 克尔医生经常说他没有发现任何新东西。

sentences.en: He's just reclaimed wisdom that's been lost to modern medicine.
sentences.zh: 他只是找回了被现代医学丢失的智慧。

sentences.en: In the past century, death moved from people's homes and into a hospital setting.
sentences.zh: 在上个世纪，死亡从人们的家中转移到了医院环境。

sentences.en: It became medicalized, with machines beeping and doctors and nurses rushing around.
sentences.zh: 它变得医疗化了，机器发出蜂鸣声，医生和护士匆忙跑来跑去。

sentences.en: And to appreciate these end-of-life experiences, you need a little bit of quiet and time to just talk.
sentences.zh: 要体会这些生命尽头的经历，你需要一点安静和时间来单纯地交谈。

sentences.en: Otherwise, they might go unnoticed.
sentences.zh: 否则，它们可能会被忽视。

sentences.en: I should say, I'm not religious.
sentences.zh: 我应该说，我不是宗教信徒。

sentences.en: I don't have beliefs about the afterlife.
sentences.zh: 我对来世没有任何信仰。

sentences.en: Normally, I write about topics like mass incarceration, abortion, or the refugee crisis.
sentences.zh: 通常，我写的是关于大规模监禁、堕胎或难民危机等话题。

sentences.en: Deathbed visions are something that I'd never heard of, until I encountered it in my own life.
sentences.zh: 临终幻象是我从未听说过的东西，直到我在自己的生活中遇到了它。

sentences.en: You'll hear about that later on.
sentences.zh: 你稍后会听到关于这方面的内容。

sentences.en: But after that experience, I was compelled to report on it.
sentences.zh: 但在那次经历之后，我不得不对此进行报道。

sentences.en: Last June, I spent about a week at Hospice Buffalo with Dr. Kerr.
sentences.zh: 去年六月，我在布法罗临终关怀医院和克尔医生呆了大约一周。

sentences.en: I met some of his patients or their surviving relatives, sitting back and letting people tell their stories.
sentences.zh: 我见到了他的一些病人或他们幸存的亲属，坐下来听人们讲述他们的故事。

sentences.en: I understand you were seeing your mom, too.
sentences.zh: 我听说你当时也看到了你的妈妈。

sentences.en: She showed up.
sentences.zh: 她出现了。

sentences.en: She was waving to you or something, right?
sentences.zh: 她朝你挥手或者做别的什么，对吧？

sentences.en: She was standing over here.
sentences.zh: 她就站在那边。

sentences.en: One patient, Peggy Holosky, said that she had been visited by her mother, who was waiting for her.
sentences.zh: 一位名叫佩吉·霍洛斯的病人说，她的母亲曾来看望她，一直在等她。

sentences.en: How long ago did she pass?
sentences.zh: 她去世多久了？

sentences.en: Eleven years.
sentences.zh: 十一年。

sentences.en: Get a smile on her face.
sentences.zh: 脸上露出了微笑。

sentences.en: You think you'll be seeing her more?
sentences.zh: 你觉得你会更多地见到她吗？

sentences.en: I will.
sentences.zh: 我会的。

sentences.en: Peggy also saw her dog.
sentences.zh: 佩吉还看到了她的狗。

sentences.en: Dr. Kerr's patients told me that being with and talking to their relatives about their visions, that it provided a kind of comfort and peace to them.
sentences.zh: 克尔医生的病人们告诉我，与亲属在一起并谈论他们的幻象，为他们提供了一种安慰和平静。

sentences.en: Their relatives said that knowing that the person they loved was not scared of what lay ahead, of death, made their grief much more bearable.
sentences.zh: 他们的亲属说，得知他们爱的人并不害怕前方等待的死亡，这让他们的悲痛变得更容易忍受。

sentences.en: Since my article was published, so many people have shared their own stories.
sentences.zh: 自从我的文章发表以来，这么多人分享了他们自己的故事。

sentences.en: Some people interpret this as evidence of an afterlife.
sentences.zh: 有些人把这解释为来世的证据。

sentences.en: Some as something about the power of our inner mind or consciousness.
sentences.zh: 有些人认为这与我们内心深处心灵或意识的力量有关。

sentences.en: Others as just love in its purest form.
sentences.zh: 还有人认为这只是最纯粹形式的爱。

sentences.en: Personally, I don't want to put a label on it myself.
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，我不想给自己贴上标签。

sentences.en: But the fact is, someday, we're all going to reach the end of our own lives.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，总有一天，我们都会走到自己生命的尽头。

sentences.en: And as the research bears out, when that does happen, people tend to find these visions helpful or spiritually meaningful.
sentences.zh: 正如研究所证实的那样，当那一刻真的发生时，人们往往会发现这些幻象是有帮助的或具有精神意义的。

sentences.en: So this story is an attempt to explain them.
sentences.zh: 所以这个故事是试图解释它们。

sentences.en: So here's my article, read by Samantha Dez.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的文章，由萨曼莎·德兹朗读。

sentences.en: Chris Kerr was 12 when he first observed a deathbed vision.
sentences.zh: 克里斯·克尔在12岁时第一次观察到临终幻象。

sentences.en: His memory of that summer in 1974 is blurred, but not the sense of mystery he felt at the bedside of his dying father.
sentences.zh: 他对1974年那个夏天的记忆已经模糊了，但在垂死的父亲床边感受到的神秘感却没有。

sentences.en: Throughout Kerr's childhood in Toronto, his father, a surgeon, was too busy to spend much time with his son, except for an annual fishing trip they took,
sentences.zh: 在克尔在多伦多的童年时期，他的父亲是一名外科医生，忙得没有太多时间陪儿子，除了他们每年进行一次的钓鱼之旅，

sentences.en: just the two of them, to the Canadian wilderness.
sentences.zh: 只有他们两个人，去加拿大荒野。

sentences.en: Caught and weakened by cancer at 42, his father reached for the buttons on Kerr's shirt, fiddled with them,
sentences.zh: 在42岁时被癌症击倒并变得虚弱，他的父亲伸手去解克尔衬衫上的纽扣，摆弄着它们，

sentences.en: and said something about getting ready to catch the plane to their cabin in the woods.
sentences.zh: 并说了一些关于准备去赶飞机去他们在树林里的木屋的话。

sentences.en: I knew intuitively.
sentences.zh: 我直觉地知道了。

sentences.en: I knew wherever he was must be a good place, because we were going fishing,
sentences.zh: 我知道无论他在哪里一定是个好地方，因为我们要去钓鱼，

sentences.en: Kerr told me.
sentences.zh: 克尔告诉我。

sentences.en: As he moved to touch his father,
sentences.zh: 当他伸手去触摸他的父亲时，

sentences.en: Kerr felt a hand on his shoulder.
sentences.zh: 克尔感觉到一只手搭在他的肩膀上。

sentences.en: A priest had followed him into the hospital room and was now leading him away, telling him his father was delusional.
sentences.zh: 一位牧师跟着他进了病房，现在正把他带走，告诉他他父亲神志不清了。

sentences.en: Kerr's father died early the next morning.
sentences.zh: 克尔的父亲于第二天清晨去世。

sentences.en: Kerr now calls what he witnessed an end-of-life vision.
sentences.zh: 克尔现在把他所目睹的称为临终幻象。

sentences.en: His father wasn't delusional, he believes.
sentences.zh: 他认为，他的父亲并非神志不清。

sentences.en: His mind was taking him to a time and place where he and his son could be together, in the wilds of northern Canada.
sentences.zh: 他的大脑把他带到了一个他和儿子可以在一起的时间和地点，在加拿大北部的荒野中。

sentences.en: And the priest, he feels, made a mistake, one that many other caregivers make, of dismissing the moment as a break with reality,
sentences.zh: 而他觉得牧师犯了一个错误，许多其他护理人员也会犯的错误，即把这一刻斥为与现实的断裂，

sentences.en: as something from which the boy required protection.
sentences.zh: 认为这是需要保护男孩免受伤害的东西。

sentences.en: It would be more than 40 years before Kerr felt compelled to speak about that evening in the hospital room.
sentences.zh: 直到40多年后，克尔才觉得有必要谈论病房里的那个晚上。

sentences.en: He had followed his father and three generations before him into medicine, and was working at Hospice and Palliative Care Buffalo, where he was the chief medical officer
sentences.zh: 他追随他的父亲以及他之前的三代人进入了医学界，并在布法罗临终关怀和姑息治疗中心工作，在那里他是首席医疗官

sentences.en: and conducted research on end-of-life visions.
sentences.zh: 并对临终幻象进行了研究。

sentences.en: It wasn't until he gave a TEDx talk in 2015 that he shared the story of his father's death.
sentences.zh: 直到他在2015年做了一场TEDx演讲，他才分享了他父亲去世的故事。

sentences.en: Pacing the stage in the sport coat he always wears, he told the audience,
sentences.zh: 他穿着他总是穿的运动外套在舞台上踱步，对观众说，

sentences.en: My point here is I didn't choose this topic of dying.
sentences.zh: 我这里的观点是我没有选择这个关于死亡的话题。

sentences.en: I feel it has chosen or followed me.
sentences.zh: 我觉得是它选择了我或跟着我。

sentences.en: He went on,
sentences.zh: 他接着说，

sentences.en: When I was present at the bedside of the dying, I was confronted by what I had seen and tried so hard to forget from my childhood.
sentences.zh: 当我出现在垂死者的病床前时，我面对的是我从童年起就看到并竭力想要忘记的东西。

sentences.en: I saw dying patients reaching and calling out to mothers and to fathers and to children, many of whom hadn't been seen for many years.
sentences.zh: 我看到垂死的病人在向母亲、父亲和孩子们伸手呼喊，其中许多人已经很多年没有见了。

sentences.en: But what was remarkable was so many of them looked at peace.
sentences.zh: 但引人注目的是，他们中的许多人看起来很平静。

sentences.en: The talk received millions of views and thousands of comments, many from nurses grateful that someone in the medical field validated what they have long understood.
sentences.zh: 这次演讲获得了数百万的浏览量和数千条评论，其中许多来自护士，他们很高兴医疗领域的某个人证实了他们长期以来所理解的东西。

sentences.en: Others, too, posted personal stories of having witnessed loved ones' visions in their final days.
sentences.zh: 其他人也发布了亲眼目睹亲人在最后日子里出现幻象的个人故事。

sentences.en: For them, Kerr's message was a kind of confirmation of something they instinctively knew, that deathbed visions are real, can provide comfort, even heal past trauma.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，克尔的信息是对他们本能就知道的事情的一种证实，即临终幻象是真实的，可以提供安慰，甚至治愈过去的创伤。

sentences.en: That they can, in some cases, feel transcendent.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，它们甚至可以让人感到超脱。

sentences.en: That our minds are capable of conjuring images that help us, at the end, make sense of our lives.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑有能力勾勒出图像，在最后帮助我们理解我们的生活。

sentences.en: Nothing in Kerr's medical training prepared him for his first shift at Hospice Buffalo one Saturday morning in the spring of 1999.
sentences.zh: 克尔在医学训练中的任何经历都没有为他1999年春季某周六早上的布法罗临终关怀医院的第一班做好准备。

sentences.en: He had earned a degree from the Medical College of Ohio while working on a Ph.D.
sentences.zh: 他在攻读神经生物学博士学位的同时，获得了俄亥俄医学院的学位。

sentences.en: in neurobiology.
sentences.zh: 在完成了内科住院医师实习后，

sentences.en: After a residency in internal medicine,
sentences.zh: 克尔在布法罗开始了心脏病学专科医师实习。

sentences.en: Kerr started a fellowship in cardiology in Buffalo.
sentences.zh: 为了赚取额外的钱来养活妻子和两个年幼的女儿，他在布法罗临终关怀医院找了一份兼职工作。

sentences.en: To earn extra money to support his wife and two young daughters, he took a part-time job with Hospice Buffalo.
sentences.zh: 在那之前，克尔一直在传统的医疗系统中工作，专注于那些常常被束缚在机器上或大量服用药物的病人。

sentences.en: Until then, Kerr had worked in the conventional medical system, focused on patients who were often tethered to machines or heavily medicated.
sentences.zh: 如果他们讲述幻象，他根本没时间去听。

sentences.en: If they recounted visions, he had no time to listen.
sentences.zh: 但在临终关怀医院的宁静中，

sentences.en: But in the quiet of Hospice,
sentences.zh: 克尔发现自己置身于一种自他父亲去世以来就再未见过的景象之中。

sentences.en: Kerr found himself in the presence of something he hadn't seen since his father's death.
sentences.zh: 病人们谈论着只有他们自己才能看到的人和地方。

sentences.en: Patients who spoke of people and places visible only to them.
sentences.zh: 所以，就像对我的父亲一样，只是一种敬畏的感觉，一种无法理解但确实感受到的东西，他说。

sentences.en: So, just like with my father, there's just this feeling of reverence, of something that wasn't understood, but certainly felt, he says.
sentences.zh: 在他的一次值班期间，

sentences.en: During one of his shifts,
sentences.zh: 克尔正在照看一位名叫玛丽的70岁妇女，她已成年的孩子们聚在她的房间里，喝着酒来活跃气氛。

sentences.en: Kerr was checking on a 70-year-old woman named Mary, whose grown children had gathered in her room, drinking wine to lighten the mood.
sentences.zh: 毫无预兆地，克尔回忆说，

sentences.en: Without warning, Kerr remembers,
sentences.zh: 玛丽在床上坐起来，双臂在胸前交叉。

sentences.en: Mary sat up in her bed and crossed her arms at her cheSt.
sentences.zh: 丹尼，她轻声呢喃着，亲吻和拥抱着一个只有她能看到的婴儿。

sentences.en: Danny, she cooed, kissing and cuddling a baby only she could see.
sentences.zh: 起初，她的孩子们感到困惑。

sentences.en: At first, her children were confused.
sentences.zh: 家里没有丹尼这个人，他们母亲的怀里也没有婴儿。

sentences.en: There was no Danny in the family, no baby in their mother's arMs.
sentences.zh: 但他们能感觉到，无论他们的母亲经历了什么，都给她带来了平静感。

sentences.en: But they could sense that whatever their mother was experiencing brought her a sense of calm.
sentences.zh: 克尔后来了解到，早在她四个孩子出生之前，

sentences.en: Kerr later learned that long before her four children were born,
sentences.zh: 玛丽在分娩时失去了一个孩子。

sentences.en: Mary lost a baby in childbirth.
sentences.zh: 她从未对孩子们提起过这件事。

sentences.en: She never spoke of it with her children.
sentences.zh: 但现在她通过一个幻象，似乎在弥补那种损失。

sentences.en: But now she was, through a vision, seemingly addressing that loss.
sentences.zh: 三十三位总统。

sentences.en: Thirty-three presidents.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打电话，他接了。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning, and he answered.
sentences.zh: 太空七十年。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星后面是什么。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 一千个消费品指南。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 今天，我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: Today, I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 六十个超级圣代。

sentences.en: Sixty super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 他们可能是联盟中每年都最好的球队。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 五万三千五百个拼图。

sentences.en: Fifty-three thousand five hundred puzzles.
sentences.zh: 我每天都使用不同的起始单词。

sentences.en: I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 两万五千个食谱。

sentences.en: Twenty-five thousand recipes.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅端食谱，因为我讨厌洗锅。

sentences.en: And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 庆祝175年来帮助您理解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，即可在 nytimes.com slash subscribe 享受特惠。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 在观察玛丽在临终关怀医院的最后日子时，

sentences.en: In observing Mary's final days at hospice,
sentences.zh: 克尔找到了他的使命。

sentences.en: Kerr found his calling.
sentences.zh: 我对医学流水线式的本质感到幻灭，

sentences.en: I was disillusioned by the assembly line nature of medicine,
sentences.zh: 克尔告诉我。

sentences.en: Kerr told me.
sentences.zh: 这感觉更像是一个人道和有尊严的护理模式。

sentences.en: This felt like a more humane and dignified model of care.
sentences.zh: 他放弃了心脏病学，全职在垂死病人的床边工作。

sentences.en: He quit cardiology to work full-time at the bedsides of dying patients.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人描述了源自他们生活并似乎具有意义的幻象，这与药物引起的幻觉或妄想、不连贯的思考不同，

sentences.en: Many of them described visions that drew from their lives and seemed to hold meaning, unlike hallucinations resulting from medication or delusional, incoherent thinking,
sentences.zh: 这些也可能发生在生命尽头。

sentences.en: which can also occur at the end of life.
sentences.zh: 但克尔无法说服其他医生，甚至是和他一起在临终关怀医院查房的年轻住院医师，让他们相信其价值。

sentences.en: But Kerr couldn't persuade other doctors, even young residents making the rounds with him at hospice, of their value.
sentences.zh: 他们想要科学证明。

sentences.en: They wanted scientific proof.
sentences.zh: 当时，只有少数已发表的医学研究记录了临终幻象，而且它们主要依赖于医生和其他护理人员的第一手报告，

sentences.en: At the time, only a handful of published medical studies had documented deathbed visions, and they largely relied on second-hand reports from doctors and other caregivers,
sentences.zh: 而不是来自病人自己的叙述。

sentences.en: rather than accounts from patients themselves.
sentences.zh: 在从会议回家的航班上，

sentences.en: On a flight home from a conference,
sentences.zh: 克尔勾勒出他自己的研究，2010年，研究员

sentences.en: Kerr outlined a study of his own, and in 2010, a research fellow,
sentences.zh: 安妮·巴尼斯加入进来与他一起进行研究。

sentences.en: Anne Banis, signed on to conduct it with him.
sentences.zh: 像克尔一样，

sentences.en: Like Kerr,
sentences.zh: 巴尼斯的家里人也有人在死前经历过幻象，她的祖父想象自己和兄弟们在火车站。

sentences.en: Banis had a family member who, before his death, experienced visions, a grandfather who imagined himself in a train station with his brothers.
sentences.zh: 这项研究并不是为了回答这些幻象在神经学上与幻觉或妄想有何不同。

sentences.en: The study wasn't designed to answer how these visions differ neurologically from hallucinations or delusions.
sentences.zh: 相反，

sentences.en: Rather,
sentences.zh: 克尔将自己的角色视为病人经历的记录者。

sentences.en: Kerr saw his role as chronicler of his patients' experiences.
sentences.zh: 借鉴社会科学研究方法，

sentences.en: Borrowing from social science research methods,
sentences.zh: 克尔、巴尼斯和他们的同事以临终关怀园区22张床位的住院部病人的每日访谈为基础进行研究，希望能捕捉到他们幻象的频率

sentences.en: Kerr, Banis, and their colleagues based their study on daily interviews with patients in the 22-bed inpatient unit at the hospice campus in the hope of capturing the frequency
sentences.zh: 和多样的主题。

sentences.en: and varied subject matter of their visions.
sentences.zh: 对病人进行了筛查，以确保他们神志清醒，没有处于混乱或谵妄状态。

sentences.en: Patients were screened to ensure that they were lucid and not in a confused or delirious state.
sentences.zh: 这项发表在2014年《姑息医学杂志》上的研究发现，幻象比其他研究人员发现的要普遍得多、频繁得多，惊人的

sentences.en: The research, published in 2014 in the Journal of Palliative Medicine, found that visions are far more common and frequent than other researchers had found, with an astonishing
sentences.zh: 88%的病人报告了至少一次幻象。

sentences.en: 88% of patients reporting at least one vision.
sentences.zh: 88%的患者报告至少出现过一次幻视。

sentences.en: Later studies in Japan,
sentences.zh: 日本、

sentences.en: India,
sentences.zh: 印度、

sentences.en: Sweden, and Australia confirm that visions are common.
sentences.zh: 瑞典和澳大利亚的后续研究证实，幻象非常普遍。

sentences.en: The percentages range from about
sentences.zh: 比例大约在

sentences.en: 20 to 80%, though a majority of these studies rely on interviews with caregivers and not patients.
sentences.zh: 20%到80%之间，不过其中大多数研究依赖于对照顾者的访谈，而非患者本人。

sentences.en: In the last 10 years,
sentences.zh: 在过去的10年里，

sentences.en: Kerr has hired a permanent research team who expanded the studies to include interviews with patients receiving hospice care at home and with their families, deepening
sentences.zh: 克尔聘请了一支常驻研究团队，将研究范围扩大到包括对接受居家临终关怀的患者及其家属的访谈，加深了

sentences.en: the researchers' understanding of the variety and profundity of these visions.
sentences.zh: 研究人员对这些幻象的多样性和深远意义的理解。

sentences.en: They can occur while patients are asleep or fully conscious.
sentences.zh: 它们可能发生在患者睡着时，也可能发生在完全清醒时。

sentences.en: Dead family members figure most prominently, and by contrast, visions involving religious themes are exceedingly rare.
sentences.zh: 逝去的家人最为显眼，相比之下，涉及宗教主题的幻象极其罕见。

sentences.en: Patients often relive seminal moments from their lives, including joyful experiences of falling in love and painful ones of rejection.
sentences.zh: 患者经常重温他们生活中的关键时刻，包括坠入爱河的快乐经历和遭受拒绝的痛苦经历。

sentences.en: Some dream of the unresolved tasks of daily life, like paying bills or raising children.
sentences.zh: 有些人会梦见日常生活中未完成的事情，比如付账单或养育孩子。

sentences.en: Visions also entail past or imagined journeys, whether long car trips or short walks to school.
sentences.zh: 幻象还包含过去或想象中的旅程，无论是长途汽车旅行还是去学校的短途散步。

sentences.en: Regardless of the subject matter, the visions, patients say, feel real and entirely unique compared with anything else they've ever experienced.
sentences.zh: 患者表示，无论主题是什么，这些幻象感觉真实，并且与他们以往经历过的任何事情都完全不同、独一无二。

sentences.en: They can begin days, even weeks, before death.
sentences.zh: 它们可以在死前几天甚至几周开始。

sentences.en: Most significant, as people near the end of their lives, the frequency of visions increases, further centering on deceased people or pets.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，随着人们临近生命终点，幻象的频率会增加，并进一步集中在死去的亲人或宠物身上。

sentences.en: It is these final visions that provide patients and their loved ones with profound meaning and solace.
sentences.zh: 正是这些最后的幻象为患者及其亲人提供了深刻的意义和慰藉。

sentences.en: Kerr's latest research is focused on the emotional transformation he has often observed in patients who experience such visions.
sentences.zh: 克尔的最新研究集中在他经常在经历此类幻象的患者身上观察到的情感转变上。

sentences.en: The first in this series of studies, published in 2019,
sentences.zh: 这一系列研究中的第一项于2019年发表，

sentences.en: measured psychological and spiritual growth among two groups of hospice patients.
sentences.zh: 测量了两组临终关怀患者的心理和精神成长：

sentences.en: those who had visions and a control group of those who did not.
sentences.zh: 一组是有幻象的患者，另一组是没有幻象的对照组。

sentences.en: Patients rated their agreement with statements including, I changed my priorities about what is important in life, or,
sentences.zh: 患者对各项陈述的赞同程度进行了评分，其中包括：我改变了对生活中重要事物的优先顺序，或者，

sentences.en: I have a better understanding of spiritual matters.
sentences.zh: 我对精神事务有了更好的理解。

sentences.en: Those who experienced end-of-life visions agreed more strongly with those statements, suggesting that the visions sparked inner change, even at the end of life.
sentences.zh: 那些经历过临终幻象的人对这些陈述表现出更强烈的赞同，这表明即使在生命终点，幻象也激发了内心的变化。

sentences.en: It's the most remarkable of our studies,
sentences.zh: 这是我们所有研究中最引人注目的，

sentences.en: Kerr told me.
sentences.zh: 克尔告诉我。

sentences.en: It highlights the paradox of dying, that while there is physical deterioration, they are growing and finding meaning.
sentences.zh: 它突显了垂死的悖论：一方面身体在退化，另一方面他们却在成长并寻找意义。

sentences.en: It highlights what patients are telling us, that they are being put back together.
sentences.zh: 它突显了患者一直在告诉我们的事情，即他们正在被重新拼凑完整。

sentences.en: In the many conversations
sentences.zh: 在过去一年中

sentences.en: Kerr and I have had over the past year, the contradiction between medicine's demand for evidence and the ineffable quality of his patients' experiences came up repeatedly.
sentences.zh: 克尔和我进行的多次对话中，医学对证据的需求与患者经历的不可言喻的特质之间的矛盾反复出现。

sentences.en: He was first struck by this tension about a year before the publication of his first study, during a visit with a World War II veteran named John, who was tormented
sentences.zh: 在发表第一项研究大约一年前，他在一次拜访一位名叫约翰的二战老兵时，首先注意到了这种紧张关系，约翰

sentences.en: throughout his life by nightmares that took him back to the beaches of Normandy on D-Day.
sentences.zh: 一生都饱受噩梦折磨，噩梦将他带回了诺曼底登陆日的诺曼底海滩。

sentences.en: John had been part of a rescue mission to bring wounded soldiers to England by ship and leave those too far gone to die.
sentences.zh: 约翰曾参与一项救援任务，用船将受伤士兵运送至英国，而将那些病入膏肓的人留在那里等死。

sentences.en: The nightmares continued through his dying days, until he dreamed of being discharged from the army.
sentences.zh: 噩梦一直持续到他濒死的日子，直到他梦见自己退伍。

sentences.en: In a second dream, a fallen soldier appeared to John to tell him that his comrades would soon come to get him.
sentences.zh: 在第二个梦中，一名阵亡士兵出现在约翰面前，告诉他他的战友很快就会来接他。

sentences.en: The nightmares ended after that.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，噩梦就结束了。

sentences.en: Kerr has been nagged ever since by the inadequacy of science and of language to fully capture the mysteries of the mind.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，科学和语言无法完全捕捉心灵奥秘的局限性一直困扰着克尔。

sentences.en: We were so caught up in trying to quantify and give structure to something so deeply spiritual and really, we were just bystanders, witnesses to this, he says.
sentences.zh: 他说：我们太沉迷于试图去量化和构建如此深刻的精神事物，而实际上，我们只是旁观者，是这一过程的见证人。

sentences.en: It feels a little small to be filling in forms when you're looking at a 90-something-year-old veteran who is back in time 70 years having an experience you can't even understand.
sentences.zh: 当你看着一个90多岁的老兵，他回到了70年前，正经历着你甚至无法理解的事情，此时却还在填写表格，这会让人觉得自己有点渺小。

sentences.en: When Kerr talks about his research at conferences, nurses tend to nod their heads in approval.
sentences.zh: 当克尔在会议上谈论他的研究时，护士们往往会点头表示赞同。

sentences.en: Doctors roll their eyes in disbelief.
sentences.zh: 医生们则不相信地翻白眼。

sentences.en: He finds that skeptics often understand the research best when they watch taped interviews with patients.
sentences.zh: 他发现，当怀疑论者观看对患者的录像访谈时，他们往往能最好地理解这项研究。

sentences.en: What's striking about this footage, which dates back to Kerr's early work in 2008, is not so much the content of the visions, but rather the patient's demeanor.
sentences.zh: 这些可以追溯到克尔2008年早期工作的录像，最引人注目的不是幻象的内容，而是患者的神态。

sentences.en: There's an absence of fear,
sentences.zh: 没有恐惧，

sentences.en: Kerr says.
sentences.zh: 克尔说。

sentences.en: A teenage girl's face lights up as she describes a dream in which she and her deceased aunt were in a castle playing with Barbie dolls.
sentences.zh: 一个十几岁女孩的脸亮了起来，她描述了一个梦，梦中她和死去的姑姑在一个城堡里玩芭比娃娃。

sentences.en: A man dying of cancer talks about his wife, who died several years earlier, and who comes to him in his dreams, always in blue.
sentences.zh: 一个因癌症垂死的男人谈到了他的妻子，她几年前去世了，总是在梦中穿着蓝色衣服来找他。

sentences.en: She waves, she smiles.
sentences.zh: 她挥手，她微笑。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: But in the moment, he seems to be transported to another time or place.
sentences.zh: 但在那一刻，他似乎被带到了另一个时间和地点。

sentences.en: At the very end, dying people lose interest in the activities that preoccupied them in life and turn toward those they love.
sentences.zh: 在最后关头，垂死的人对生前使他们全神贯注的活动失去了兴趣，转而面向他们所爱的人。

sentences.en: As to why,
sentences.zh: 至于原因，

sentences.en: Kerr can only speculate.
sentences.zh: 克尔只能推测。

sentences.en: In his 2020 book,
sentences.zh: 在他的2020年著作

sentences.en: Death is But a Dream, he concludes that the love his patients find in dying often brings them to a place that some call enlightenment and others call God.
sentences.zh: 《死亡不过是一场梦》（Death is But a Dream）中，他得出结论：患者在垂死之际找到的爱，常常将他们带到一个有些人称之为开悟、有些人称之为上帝的境地。

sentences.en: Time seems to vanish, he told me.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，时间似乎消失了。

sentences.en: The people who loved you well, secured you, and contributed to who you are are still accessible at a spiritual and psychological level.
sentences.zh: 那些深爱着你、给予你安全感、并造就了现在的你的人，在精神和心理层面上依然是可以触及的。

sentences.en: That was the case with Connor O'Neill, who died at the age of 10 in 2022, and whose parents,
sentences.zh: 康纳·奥尼尔（Connor O'Neill）的情况就是如此，他在2022年以10岁的年龄去世，他的父母，

sentences.en: Kerr and I, visited in their home.
sentences.zh: 克尔和我曾去他们家中拜访过。

sentences.en: They told us that just two days before his death, their son called out the name of a family friend who, without the boy's knowledge, had just died.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我们，就在他去世前两天，他们的儿子喊出了一个家庭朋友的名字，而这个朋友刚刚去世，男孩并不知道这件事。

sentences.en: Do you know where you are?
sentences.zh: 你知道你在哪儿吗？

sentences.en: Connor's mother asked.
sentences.zh: 康纳的母亲问。

sentences.en: Heaven, the boy replied.
sentences.zh: 天堂，男孩回答。

sentences.en: Connor had barely spoken in days or moved without help.
sentences.zh: 康纳已经好几天几乎没说过话，没有别人的帮助也无法移动。

sentences.en: But in that moment, he sat up under his own strength and threw his arms around her neck.
sentences.zh: 但在那一刻，他凭着自己的力量坐了起来，双手搂住了她的脖子。

sentences.en: Mommy, I love you, he said.
sentences.zh: 妈咪，我爱你，他说。

sentences.en: Kerr's research finds that such moments, which transcend the often painful physical decline in the last days of life, help parents like the O'Neills and other relatives grieve even
sentences.zh: 克尔的研究发现，这些超越了生命最后几天往往痛苦的身体衰退的时刻，帮助像奥尼尔一家这样的父母和其他亲属去哀悼

sentences.en: unfathomable loss.
sentences.zh: 那无法想象的失落。

sentences.en: I don't know where I would be without that closure or that gift that was given to us,
sentences.zh: 康纳的父亲告诉我们：如果没有那种释怀，或者说没有给予我们的那种礼物，我不知道我现在会在哪里。

sentences.en: Connor's father told us.
sentences.zh: 就算有了这些，日子也已经够难的了。

sentences.en: It's hard enough with it.
sentences.zh: 正如克尔所解释的，这就是受伤与被抚慰之间的区别。

sentences.en: As Kerr explains, it's the difference between being wounded and soothed.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜露（Winnalou）。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我编写了游戏

sentences.en: I write the game
sentences.zh: 《连线》（Connections），这是《纽约时报》游戏中的谜题之一，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，我喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基（Sam Mazursky），我每天都创作

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game
sentences.zh: 《拼字比赛》（Spelling Bee）和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉（promesthesia）的东西。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚才听到的那些人一样。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com 加上 games，今天就开始游玩吧。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 在六月，

sentences.en: In June,
sentences.zh: 我拜访了一名患者的成年女儿，她的母亲几天前刚刚在家中去世。

sentences.en: I visited the adult daughter of a patient who died at home just days earlier.
sentences.zh: 我们坐在她母亲的客厅里，望向天井和喂鸟器，这些曾给母亲带来如此多的欢乐。

sentences.en: We sat in her mother's living room, looking out on the patio and bird feeders that had given the mother so much joy.
sentences.zh: 在母亲去世前三天，女儿正在收拾房间，这时母亲开始说话，比她几天来的任何时候都要清醒。

sentences.en: Three days before her mother's death, the daughter was straightening up the room when her mother began to speak more lucidly than she had in days.
sentences.zh: 女儿爬进母亲的床，握住她的手，静静聆听。

sentences.en: The daughter crawled into her mother's bed, held her hand, and listened.
sentences.zh: 母亲首先和女儿的父亲说话，她能看到他在房间的角落里，一如既往地帅气。

sentences.en: Her mother first spoke to the daughter's father, whom she could see in the far corner of the room, handsome as ever.
sentences.zh: 然后她开始和她的第二任丈夫说话，只有她能看见他，但对女儿来说却足够真实，甚至问他是否在抽烟斗。

sentences.en: She then started speaking with her second husband, visible only to her, yet real enough for the daughter to ask whether he was smoking his pipe.
sentences.zh: 你闻不到吗？

sentences.en: Can't you smell it?
sentences.zh: 母亲回答说。

sentences.en: Her mother replied.
sentences.zh: 即使在重述时，那一刻也感觉神圣。

sentences.en: Even in the retelling, the moment felt sacred.
sentences.zh: 女儿对我说：我永远、永远不会忘记它。

sentences.en: I will never, ever forget it, the daughter told me.
sentences.zh: 它是如此美丽。

sentences.en: It was so beautiful.
sentences.zh: 我还见到了巴尼斯（Banis）的一位患者，

sentences.en: I also met one of Banis' patients,
sentences.zh: 佩吉·霍洛斯基（Peggy Holosky）。几天前，布法罗癌症医院的医生发现她全身都有血栓，

sentences.en: Peggy Holosky, who had enrolled in hospice for home care services just days earlier after doctors at the cancer hospital in Buffalo found blood clots throughout her body,
sentences.zh: 这表明为期一年的治疗已经失效，于是她登记加入了临终关怀的居家服务。

sentences.en: a sign that the year-long treatment had stopped working.
sentences.zh: 是时候让她的丈夫

sentences.en: It was time for her husband,
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬（Stephen）和他们的两只灵缇犬一起，让她在家中过得舒适了。

sentences.en: Stephen, to keep her comfortable at home with their two greyhounds.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬带领巴尼斯和我来到家庭活动室，佩吉正躺在沙发上。

sentences.en: Stephen led Banis and me to the family room where Peggy lay on the couch.
sentences.zh: 巴尼斯跪在地板上，检查了患者的导尿管，减少了她的处方药，这样她每天要吞咽的药丸就变少了，并开了一种用于缓解尾骨疼痛的

sentences.en: Banis knelt on the floor, checked her patient's catheter, reduced her prescriptions so there were fewer pills for her to swallow every day, and ordered a numbing cream
sentences.zh: 麻醉膏。

sentences.en: for pain in her tailbone.
sentences.zh: 她还询问了关于幻象的事。

sentences.en: She also asked about her visions.
sentences.zh: 那个周末值班的护士目睹了佩吉与她死去的母亲说话。

sentences.en: The nurse on call that weekend witnessed Peggy speaking with her dead mother.
sentences.zh: 她就站在那边，

sentences.en: She was standing over here,
sentences.zh: 佩吉对巴尼斯说，手势指向房间的角落。

sentences.en: Peggy told Banis, gesturing toward the corner of the room.
sentences.zh: 那是你唯一一次看到她吗？

sentences.en: Was that the only time you saw her?
sentences.zh: 巴尼斯问。

sentences.en: Banis asked.
sentences.zh: 目前是。

sentences.en: So far.
sentences.zh: 你觉得你以后还会经常看到她吗？

sentences.en: Do you think you'll be seeing her more?
sentences.zh: 我会的。

sentences.en: I will.
sentences.zh: 考虑到目前的情况，我会的。

sentences.en: I will, considering what's going on.
sentences.zh: 佩吉深深地陷进沙发里，闭上眼睛，回忆起另一次死者的造访，这一次是她和斯蒂芬收养的第一只灵缇犬。

sentences.en: Peggy sank deeper into the couch and closed her eyes, recounting another visit from the dead, this time by the first greyhound she and Stephen adopted.
sentences.zh: 我和所有人都释怀了。

sentences.en: I'm at peace with everybody.
sentences.zh: 我很幸福，她说。

sentences.en: I'm happy, she said.
sentences.zh: 时间还未到。

sentences.en: It's not time yet.
sentences.zh: 我知道时间还未到，但它快要到了。

sentences.en: I know it's not time, but it's coming.
sentences.zh: 当我的母亲

sentences.en: When my mother,
sentences.zh: 克洛伊·泽维克（Chloe Zerwick）于2018年濒死时，

sentences.en: Chloe Zerwick, was dying in 2018,
sentences.zh: 我从未听说过临终幻象。

sentences.en: I had never heard of end-of-life visions.
sentences.zh: 当她的照顾者开始向我讲述我们当时称之为幻觉的事情时，我完全是凭直觉行事。

sentences.en: I was acting on intuition when her caregiver started telling me about what we were then calling hallucinations.
sentences.zh: 妈妈当时95岁，患有肺病和充血性心力衰竭，在哈德逊河谷的家中接受临终关怀，几乎无法离开床榻。

sentences.en: Mom was 95 and living in her Hudson Valley home under hospice care with lung disease and congestive heart failure, barely able to leave her bed.
sentences.zh: 临终关怀医生给她开了一种用于止痛的阿片类药物，并让她服用抗精神病和抗焦虑药物，以控制他所担心的会阻止

sentences.en: The hospice doctor prescribed an opioid for pain and put her on antipsychotic and anti-anxiety medicines to tame the so-called hallucinations he worried were preventing
sentences.zh: 她入睡的所谓幻觉。

sentences.en: her from sleeping.
sentences.zh: 这些药物中的一部分可能导致了妈妈的幻象。

sentences.en: It is possible that some of these medications caused mom's visions.
sentences.zh: 但正如克尔所解释的那样，药物引起的幻觉并不排除自然发生的幻象。

sentences.en: But as Kerr has explained, drug-induced hallucinations do not rule out naturally occurring visions.
sentences.zh: 它们可以共存。

sentences.en: They can coexiSt.
sentences.zh: 在我母亲的案例中，我内心里明白，她虚构的生活是需要去尊重的。

sentences.en: In my mother's case, I inherently understood that her imaginary life was something to honor.
sentences.zh: 我知道药物引起的幻觉看起来和感觉起来是什么样的。

sentences.en: I knew what medicine-induced hallucinations looked and felt like.
sentences.zh: 在她去世大约10年前，妈妈摔倒并伤到了脊椎。

sentences.en: About 10 years before her death, mom fell and injured her spine.
sentences.zh: 当地医院的医生给她使用了阿片类药物来控制疼痛，这让她表现得像变了一个人。

sentences.en: Doctors in the local hospital put her on an opioid to control the pain, which left her acting like a different person.
sentences.zh: 她说，有蜘蛛在医院的墙上爬行。

sentences.en: There were spiders crawling on the hospital wall, she said.
sentences.zh: 她把室友的床错当成了火车站台。

sentences.en: She mistook her roommate's bed for a train platform.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，她否认我爱她，或者曾经爱过她。

sentences.en: Worse, she denied that I loved her or ever did.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们让她停药，幻觉就消失了。

sentences.en: Once we took her off the medicine, the hallucinations vanished.
sentences.zh: 她在生命尽头经历的幻象则完全不同。

sentences.en: The visions she was having at the end of her life were entirely different.
sentences.zh: 它们与她度过漫长一生息息相关，并带来了深深的安慰和愉悦。

sentences.en: They were connected to the long life she had led and brought a deep sense of comfort and delight.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我一生中第一次没有了任何担忧，她对我说。

sentences.en: You know, for the first time in my life, I have no worries, she told me.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时感觉卸下了千斤重担。

sentences.en: I remember feeling a weight lift.
sentences.zh: 在健康状况恶化了十多年之后，她似乎找到了平静感。

sentences.en: After more than a decade of failing health, she seemed to have found a sense of peace.
sentences.zh: 在她去世的前一天，随着呼吸变得更加困难，妈妈发布了一个消息。

sentences.en: The day before her death, as her breathing became more labored, mom made an announcement.
sentences.zh: 我有了一个新领路人，她说。

sentences.en: I have a new leader, she said.
sentences.zh: 那是谁？

sentences.en: Who is that?
sentences.zh: 我问。

sentences.en: I asked.
sentences.zh: 马克。

sentences.en: Mark.
sentences.zh: 他要带我去另一边。

sentences.en: He's going to take me to the other side.
sentences.zh: 她说的是我的丈夫，他当时在北卡罗来纳州的家中活得好好的。

sentences.en: She was speaking of my husband, alive and well back home in North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 太棒了，妈妈，只是我需要他留在这里陪我，我回答道。

sentences.en: That's great, mom, except that I need him here with me, I replied.
sentences.zh: 你觉得他能两边兼顾吗？

sentences.en: Do you think he can do both?
sentences.zh: 哦，能的，他非常有能力。

sentences.en: Oh, yes, he's very capable.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，他非常能干。

sentences.en: That evening, mom was struggling again to breathe.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上，妈妈再次呼吸困难。

sentences.en: I'm thinking of the next world, she said, and of my husband, who would lead her there.
sentences.zh: 她说，我在想着另一个世界，想着我的丈夫，他会领着我去那里。

sentences.en: The caregiver on duty for the night and I sat at her bedside as mom's oxygen level fell from 68 to 63 to 52 and kept dropping until she died the next morning.
sentences.zh: 夜班护理员和我坐在她床边，看着妈妈的血氧水平从68跌到63，又跌到52，一路下降，直到第二天早晨她离世。

sentences.en: My mother was not a brave person in the traditional sense of the word.
sentences.zh: 传统意义上，我的母亲并不是一个勇敢的人。

sentences.en: She was afraid of snakes, the subway platform, and any hint of pain.
sentences.zh: 她害怕蛇、地铁站台，以及任何一丝疼痛。

sentences.en: But she faced her death confident that a man who loves her daughter would guide her to whatever lay ahead.
sentences.zh: 但她笃信一个深爱她女儿的男人会指引她走向未知的世界，并从容地面对死亡。

sentences.en: Do you think it will happen to you?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这种事会发生在你身上吗？

sentences.en: She asked me at one point about her dreaming life.
sentences.zh: 她一度向我问起她的梦境生活。

sentences.en: Maybe it's genetic, I replied, not knowing, as I do now, that these experiences are part of what may await us all.
sentences.zh: 也许这是遗传的吧，我回答道，当时并不知道，正如我现在所知的那样，这些经历或许是我们所有人终将面临的一部分。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目中，我们正为假期的亲友接待做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人们宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们对光线敏感而无法入睡吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们喝到断片才去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线条件，因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏史或食物不耐受吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》App或你喜欢的任何播客平台上搜索《Wirecutter秀》。
